questions.q: How does a data standard differ from a data policy?
options: A standard provides the concrete, technical detail that implements the policy's high-level requirement
Only executives are allowed to read standards, while anyone can read a policy
A standard always overrides and replaces its related policy
A standard and a policy are exactly the same thing with different names
questions.explain: The policy states what is required and why; the standard specifies the exact, checkable rule that implements it.

questions.q: In this lesson's example, 'all customer account numbers must be 10 digits, starting with two letters identifying the region' is an example of:
options: A format standard
A RACI matrix
A governance committee charter
An executive sponsorship statement
questions.explain: This is a concrete structural specification for a field — a textbook format standard, implementing the confidentiality policy from the previous lesson.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four standard categories described in this lesson?
options: Marketing standards
Format standards
Terminology standards
Quality standards
questions.explain: The four categories covered are format, terminology, quality, and security standards — not 'marketing standards.'

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a policy with no standard is 'too vague to apply consistently'?
options: Because standards are legally required documents while policies are optional
Without a concrete, checkable rule, teams have no consistent way to verify whether the policy's requirement is actually being met
Because policies are never read by anyone once written
Because a policy automatically becomes a standard after 90 days
questions.explain: A policy states intent; without a standard's concrete specification, there's no consistent way to check if that intent is being honored.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where does most day-to-day governance friction actually tend to live?
options: In the policies — almost nobody disputes high-level statements like 'customer data should be confidential'
In the standards — the specific thresholds, formats, and naming conventions people argue over
Exclusively in executive sponsorship decisions
Nowhere — governance programs never generate any friction
questions.explain: People rarely dispute broad policy statements; the real arguments are over whose format, threshold, or convention wins at the standard level.
